title: Channel Configuration
description: Sets up DMA channels with source, destination, transfer size, and trigger source, matching each peripheral to its channel's capabilities. Correct configuration is the difference between effortless streaming and silent data corruption.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Burst Transfers
description: Moves data in bursts that hold the bus for several beats, amortizing arbitration overhead across many words. Bursts dramatically raise throughput for bulk moves like frame buffers and audio streams.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Scatter-Gather
description: Chains descriptors so one DMA operation gathers from scattered buffers or scatters to them, without CPU intervention between pieces. Scatter-gather handles real-world fragmented buffers at full hardware speed.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Double Buffering
description: Alternates between two buffers - the DMA fills one while the CPU processes the other - giving continuous streaming with no gaps. Double buffering is the standard pattern for audio, video, and sensor capture.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: DMA Descriptors
description: Describes each transfer - addresses, counts, control flags - in memory structures the DMA engine walks itself. Well-designed descriptors let the engine run whole transfer programs autonomously.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Arbitration
description: Decides which DMA channel gets the bus when several request at once, using priorities or round-robin. Fair arbitration keeps one greedy channel from starving the others.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Cache Coherency
description: Keeps CPU caches and DMA in agreement - flushing before DMA reads, invalidating after DMA writes - so neither sees stale data. Coherency handling is the subtle art that makes DMA correct on cached systems.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Transfer Completion IRQs
description: Interrupts the CPU when a DMA transfer finishes or errors, so software learns promptly without polling. Completion interrupts with error flags distinguish success from the many ways transfers fail.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Circular Buffers
description: Runs DMA around a ring buffer with head/tail pointers, giving endless streaming with fixed memory. Circular buffers with DMA are the backbone of continuous capture - audio, radio, telemetry.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Peripheral Mapping
description: Maps each peripheral's data register to its DMA channel and trigger, often through a configurable crossbar. Correct mapping tables are board-specific knowledge that must match the datasheet exactly.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Error Handling
description: Detects and recovers from DMA errors - bus faults, descriptor errors, timeouts - with clear status reporting. Robust error handling turns DMA from fragile magic into a dependable subsystem.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Bandwidth Allocation
description: Reserves bus bandwidth per channel so critical streams - display, audio - never glitch even when bulk transfers saturate the bus. Allocation turns best-effort DMA into guaranteed-quality streaming.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Chained Transfers
description: Links transfers so the completion of one triggers the next without CPU involvement, building autonomous multi-stage pipelines. Chains move data through processing stages - capture, filter, store - entirely in hardware.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Memory-to-Memory DMA
description: Uses the DMA engine for bulk memory copies and fills, freeing the CPU for real work. Mem-to-mem DMA with the right burst settings beats CPU copy loops on both speed and power.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: DMA Security
description: Restricts which memory DMA engines may touch through IOMMU or MPU regions, so a misprogrammed peripheral cannot read or corrupt arbitrary RAM. DMA security boundaries are essential wherever untrusted devices exist.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
